Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

aiTitle: A* plan 的 max_cost 参数

content.content:
1	# Route Planner
2	
3	A dependency-free Python reference implementation for robotics, path-planning, a-star.
4	
5	Run with: python3 demo.py
6	Tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
7	
8	## Scope
9	
10	实现一个确定性的二维栅格 A* 路径规划器。规划器支持障碍物、四邻域移动、固定的 tie-break 规则和不可达结果；返回路径、总代价及扩展节点统计，不能越过障碍或产生重复节点。公开数据结构和边界行为应当适合离线回放，后续可在同一基线上扩展代价地图和动态障碍处理。
11	
12	## API 约定
13	
14	`plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)` 默认返回 `{"path", "cost", "expanded"}`；`trace=True` 时额外返回 `expanded_nodes`；提供 `max_expanded` 时额外返回 `status`；`snapshot=True` 且因预算耗尽返回 `budget_exhausted` 时额外返回 `checkpoint`。
15	
16	**搜索预算（`max_expanded`）**
17	- `max_expanded` 省略或为 `None` 时，返回键、值、异常类型与校验顺序与既有行为完全一致。提供时必须是非负且非布尔的整数：其他类型抛 `TypeError`，负数抛 `ValueError`；这些校验在全部既有网格、`costs`、`trace` 与 `dynamic_blocked` 校验（含第 0 帧检查）完成之后、搜索开始前进行。
18	- 预算按关闭节点数计（即 `expanded` 的计数口径），达到上限后不再关闭任何节点。提供预算时结果始终额外携带 `status`：目标在限额内关闭为 `"found"`（返回既有的 `path`/`cost`）；候选耗尽仍未到达目标为 `"unreachable"`；尚有候选但预算耗尽为 `"budget_exhausted"`（`path`/`cost` 为 `None`，`expanded` 为实际关闭数，不超过 `max_expanded`）。
19	- 预算对静态与动态模式同样生效，且不改变扩展顺序、路径选择、轨迹条目或确定性：带预算的轨迹是无预算轨迹的前缀。`trace=True` 时只记录实际关闭的节点，预算为零时即使 `start == goal` 也返回 `budget_exhausted`（`expanded` 为 0，`expanded_nodes` 为空）；单点成功结果要求至少关闭一个节点（`max_expanded >= 1`）。
20	- `replay` 不受预算影响：不接受预算参数，仍只校验候选路径。
21	
22	`plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)` 接受与 `plan` 相同的网格、`blocked`、`start` 及可选代价、轨迹、动态障碍、预算和快照参数，另收一个非空 `goals` 候选终点序列，返回一条确定的最低代价路线（返回结构与 `plan` 相同，`path` 末点为选中的候选终点）；该路径可直接以其末点作为 `goal` 交给 `replay` 离线核验。
23	
24	**多终点（`goals`）**
25	- 外层必须是非空序列：字符串、字节串、`None` 或其他非序列抛 `TypeError`，空序列抛 `ValueError`。每个终点沿用坐标的结构和整数规则：元素形状或坐标类型不合格抛 `TypeError`，越界或落在静态障碍上抛 `ValueError`。`goals` 在 `plan` 校验序列中占据 `goal` 的位置，网格、`costs`、`trace`、`dynamic_blocked` 与预算的校验顺序及异常类型沿用 `plan`；`start` 仍须通过静态障碍与动态第 0 帧检查。
26	- 重复候选点合并，输入排列（以及 `blocked`、帧内坐标的迭代顺序）不影响任何结果。
27	- 候选终点在某条路线到达的时间帧被动态障碍阻挡时不在输入阶段报错：该路线按其时间帧不可达，其他到达时刻仍可参与竞争；末帧之后持续使用最后一帧。
28	- 搜索保留四邻域移动、禁止等待和回访、进入格子的代价累计。总 `cost` 最小者优先；同价时先比较终点坐标 `(x, y)` 字典序，再比较完整路径字典序。与动态 `plan` 同理，经不同历史到达同一格子的路线是不同状态、互不剪枝；`trace` 在静态模式记录坐标二元组、动态模式记录 `(x, y, t)` 三元组，且只记录实际关闭的节点。
29	- 没有任何可行终点时 `path`/`cost` 为 `None`；提供预算时按既有规则返回 `status` 为 `found`、`unreachable` 或 `budget_exhausted`，预算不会把已确定的较优路线替换成严格次优（更贵）的路线。`goals` 含 `start` 时按既有 `start == goal` 单点零代价规则处理（零预算同样为 `budget_exhausted`）。
30	
31	`replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None, dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)` 用于离线核验一条已保存的候选路径并重新计算代价；它不执行搜索，返回值不含 `expanded` 或 `expanded_nodes` 字段，且不接受 `trace` 参数。
32	
33	**快照与恢复（`snapshot` 与 `resume`）**
34	- `snapshot` 只能是布尔值，默认 `False`；省略或为 `False` 时 `plan`/`plan_any` 的返回键、值、异常类型、校验顺序、tie-break、不可达结果与轨迹完全不变。非布尔值在全部既有校验（含 `max_expanded` 校验）之后、搜索开始前抛 `TypeError`。
35	- `snapshot=True` 且本次搜索因达到 `max_expanded` 上限返回 `budget_exhausted` 时，结果额外携带 `checkpoint`；已找到终点或确认不可达的结果不生成该字段。`checkpoint` 只含可 JSON 序列化的值：快照版本、规划器类型（`"plan"`/`"plan_any"`）、规范化网格约束（尺寸、障碍、起终点或候选终点、`costs`、`dynamic_blocked`）、已关闭节点计数、至此的轨迹以及待处理候选的完整状态；所有由集合派生的列表均排序存储，键与值的顺序不受集合迭代、目标列表或帧内坐标顺序影响，调用方可原样保存后传回 `resume`。
36	- `resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)` 按快照继续同一确定性搜索。`max_expanded` 仍表示从起点累计允许关闭的节点总数：上限不大于已关闭数时不再关闭任何节点。恢复结果的 `path`、`cost`、`expanded`、`status`（仅在提供 `max_expanded` 时返回）与 `expanded_nodes`（恢复结果始终返回；静态模式记录坐标二元组，动态模式记录 `(x, y, t)` 三元组）等价于一次未暂停的调用，重复恢复不会重复计入已关闭节点。再次达到上限时返回新的 `checkpoint`，可继续恢复；最终 `found` 或 `unreachable` 时省略它。恢复成功的路径可直接交给 `replay` 并得到相同代价与步数。
37	- 校验：`checkpoint` 不是对象、缺少必要字段或字段类型不对时抛 `TypeError`；快照版本、规划器类型、网格约束、障碍、起终点、候选终点、`costs`、`dynamic_blocked` 或内部状态不一致时统一抛 `ValueError`；所有错误在搜索前确定。`resume` 的 `max_expanded` 复用 `plan` 的非负整数规则（其他类型抛 `TypeError`，负数抛 `ValueError`）。
38	
39	**诊断模式（`diagnose=True`）**
40	- `diagnose` 只能是布尔值；省略或为 `False` 时，`replay` 的返回键、值、异常类型与校验顺序与默认行为完全一致。非布尔值在全部网格校验（含动态第零帧）完成后、`path` 结构检查之前抛出 `TypeError`。
41	- 传 `True` 且结构合法时，有效路径仍返回 `valid`、`cost`、`steps`，并额外返回 `"error": None, "error_index": None`；`cost` 仍按进入格子规则重算，`steps == len(path) - 1`。
42	- 无效路径仍不抛异常，`cost`、`steps` 为 `None`，并返回唯一的 `error` 及首个违规元素的零基 `path` 下标。按固定优先级（同一点同时满足多项时取最前者，且不返回任何部分累计代价）：
43	  - `start_mismatch`：首点不是 `start`，下标 0；
44	  - `goal_mismatch`：末点不是 `goal`，下标为末点（`len(path) - 1`）；
45	  - `start_goal_extra`：`start == goal` 却含多余点，下标 1；
46	  - `repeated_coordinate`：重复坐标，指向第二次出现的位置；
47	  - `non_adjacent`：相邻点不是四邻域移动，指向后一个点；
48	  - `static_blocked`：经过静态障碍，指向该点；
49	  - `dynamic_blocked`：在对应时间帧（或持续使用的末帧）中被禁行，指向该点。
50	
51	**replay 返回结构**
52	- 路径合规时返回 `{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}`：`steps` 为移动边数，恒等于 `len(path) - 1`（`start == goal` 的单点路径为 0）；`cost` 按 `plan` 既有的进入格子规则重算，即路径所进入格子的代价之和，未提供 `costs` 时每步为 1，提供时起点代价不计入，因此与 `plan` 对同一路径给出的代价一致。
53	- 路径语义不合规时不抛异常，固定返回 `{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`，不返回任何部分累计值。不合规情形包括：未从 `start` 开始、未在 `goal` 结束、经过静态障碍、经过路径下标 `t` 对应的动态障碍帧、相邻点不是四邻域移动、出现重复坐标，以及 `start == goal` 却包含多余点。
54	- 合规判定与动态时间索引：`dynamic_blocked` 省略、为 `None` 或为空序列时按静态模式检查；否则路径下标 `t` 处的坐标必须避开第 `t` 帧，超过最后一帧后持续使用最后一帧（与 `plan` 的索引规则一致）。
55	
56	**replay 异常边界（校验先于路径判定）**
57	- 网格参数（`width`、`height`、`blocked`、`start`、`goal`、`costs`、`dynamic_blocked`）沿用 `plan` 的公开校验与既有 `TypeError`/`ValueError` 边界及顺序，包括 `start` 落在静态障碍或第 0 帧时抛出 `ValueError`；这些校验全部在检查 `path` 之前完成。
58	- `path` 必须是非空坐标序列：字符串、字节串、`None` 或其他非序列抛出 `TypeError`；空序列抛出 `TypeError`；元素不是恰好两个整数（含长度不为二、非整数、布尔坐标）抛出 `TypeError`；坐标越界抛出 `ValueError`。
59	- 仅语义上无效（结构合法但不满足上述合规条件）的路径不抛异常，返回固定的无效结构。
60	
61	**plan 输入校验（搜索开始前完成）** —— replay 的网格参数沿用同一套校验：
62	- `width`、`height` 必须为正整数。
63	- `start`、`goal` 及 `blocked` 中每个元素必须是两个整数构成的坐标（元组或长度为二的列表等序列，统一规范化为元组）。
64	- `costs` 可省略或为 `None`（单位代价）；否则必须是 `height` 行、`width` 列的正整数矩阵（按行排列，`costs[y][x]` 为进入格子 `(x, y)` 的代价）。字符串/字节串、非整数单元格、布尔值抛出 `TypeError`；行数或列数不符、代价非正抛出 `ValueError`。
65	- `trace` 必须为布尔值，其他类型在搜索开始前抛出 `TypeError`。
66	- 类型或结构不符抛出 `TypeError`；尺寸非正、坐标越界、端点落在障碍物上抛出 `ValueError`。
67	- `blocked` 中的重复坐标被合并，不影响结果。
68	
69	**搜索语义**
70	- 四邻域移动，曼哈顿启发式。未提供 `costs` 时为单位步长代价；提供时进入格子的代价为该格的值，起点代价不计入，`cost` 等于路径所进入格子的代价之和。
71	- 平局次序固定且公开：先比较 f，再比较 h，再按 (x, y) 字典序；结果不依赖 `blocked` 的迭代顺序。
72	- `expanded` 只统计从优先队列取出并首次关闭的节点；成功时计入 goal，`start == goal` 时返回单节点路径、代价 0、`expanded` 为 1；不可达时 `path`/`cost` 为 `None`，`expanded` 等于实际关闭的可通行节点数。
73	
74	**搜索轨迹（`trace=True`）**
75	- 成功与不可达结果都额外返回 `expanded_nodes`：坐标元组构成的序列，按节点首次计入 `expanded` 的顺序记录，包含 `start`；成功时包含 `goal`，不可达时记录搜索结束前关闭的全部可通行节点。
76	- `expanded_nodes` 不含未扩展项、重复坐标或障碍物，且恒有 `expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`；`start == goal` 时序列只有一个坐标。
77	- `trace=False` 或省略时返回对象不含该字段，其余键、值与校验顺序与默认行为完全一致。
78	
79	**动态障碍（`dynamic_blocked`）**
80	- `dynamic_blocked` 省略、为 `None` 或为空序列时与未启用完全等价；否则必须是按时间帧排列的序列，每一帧是该帧禁行坐标的可迭代集合。第 0 帧约束 `start`，路径下标 `t` 处的坐标必须同时避开静态障碍和第 `t` 帧，超过最后一帧后持续使用最后一帧。
81	- 每一步仍只能向四邻域移动，不允许原地等待或重复坐标；`cost` 仍按进入格子的代价累计，起点不计。由于路线的可延续性取决于它已访问的坐标序列，到达同一 `(x, y, t)` 但历史不同的候选是不同状态，互不剪枝：所有满足约束的路线都能被搜索到。
82	- 返回总代价最小的可行路径；总代价相同时，固定优先级依次为 f、h、x、y、t，仍相同时按完整坐标路径的字典序决定取舍，因此结果不依赖障碍集合、帧内坐标顺序或遍历顺序。
83	- 动态模式下 `expanded_nodes` 按实际关闭顺序记录 `(x, y, t)` 三元组，`expanded` 按条目计数；被丢弃的候选不记录。同一 `(x, y, t)` 若由不同历史分别关闭，其三元组按关闭顺序分别出现，`expanded` 逐条计数。不可达时 `path`/`cost` 为 `None`。
84	- 校验：外层必须是序列，每一帧必须是可迭代坐标集合；字符串/字节串、非二整数坐标抛出 `TypeError`，越界坐标抛出 `ValueError`，帧内重复坐标合并；`start` 在第 0 帧被禁止时抛出 `ValueError`。所有校验在搜索开始前完成，既有校验顺序不变。

# Route Planner

A dependency-free Python reference implementation for robotics, path-planning, a-star.

Run with: python3 demo.py
Tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Scope

实现一个确定性的二维栅格 A* 路径规划器。规划器支持障碍物、四邻域移动、固定的 tie-break 规则和不可达结果；返回路径、总代价及扩展节点统计，不能越过障碍或产生重复节点。公开数据结构和边界行为应当适合离线回放，后续可在同一基线上扩展代价地图和动态障碍处理。

## API 约定

`plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)` 默认返回 `{"path", "cost", "expanded"}`；`trace=True` 时额外返回 `expanded_nodes`；提供 `max_expanded` 时额外返回 `status`；`snapshot=True` 且因预算耗尽返回 `budget_exhausted` 时额外返回 `checkpoint`。

**搜索预算（`max_expanded`）**
- `max_expanded` 省略或为 `None` 时，返回键、值、异常类型与校验顺序与既有行为完全一致。提供时必须是非负且非布尔的整数：其他类型抛 `TypeError`，负数抛 `ValueError`；这些校验在全部既有网格、`costs`、`trace` 与 `dynamic_blocked` 校验（含第 0 帧检查）完成之后、搜索开始前进行。
- 预算按关闭节点数计（即 `expanded` 的计数口径），达到上限后不再关闭任何节点。提供预算时结果始终额外携带 `status`：目标在限额内关闭为 `"found"`（返回既有的 `path`/`cost`）；候选耗尽仍未到达目标为 `"unreachable"`；尚有候选但预算耗尽为 `"budget_exhausted"`（`path`/`cost` 为 `None`，`expanded` 为实际关闭数，不超过 `max_expanded`）。
- 预算对静态与动态模式同样生效，且不改变扩展顺序、路径选择、轨迹条目或确定性：带预算的轨迹是无预算轨迹的前缀。`trace=True` 时只记录实际关闭的节点，预算为零时即使 `start == goal` 也返回 `budget_exhausted`（`expanded` 为 0，`expanded_nodes` 为空）；单点成功结果要求至少关闭一个节点（`max_expanded >= 1`）。
- `replay` 不受预算影响：不接受预算参数，仍只校验候选路径。

`plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)` 接受与 `plan` 相同的网格、`blocked`、`start` 及可选代价、轨迹、动态障碍、预算和快照参数，另收一个非空 `goals` 候选终点序列，返回一条确定的最低代价路线（返回结构与 `plan` 相同，`path` 末点为选中的候选终点）；该路径可直接以其末点作为 `goal` 交给 `replay` 离线核验。

**多终点（`goals`）**
- 外层必须是非空序列：字符串、字节串、`None` 或其他非序列抛 `TypeError`，空序列抛 `ValueError`。每个终点沿用坐标的结构和整数规则：元素形状或坐标类型不合格抛 `TypeError`，越界或落在静态障碍上抛 `ValueError`。`goals` 在 `plan` 校验序列中占据 `goal` 的位置，网格、`costs`、`trace`、`dynamic_blocked` 与预算的校验顺序及异常类型沿用 `plan`；`start` 仍须通过静态障碍与动态第 0 帧检查。
- 重复候选点合并，输入排列（以及 `blocked`、帧内坐标的迭代顺序）不影响任何结果。
- 候选终点在某条路线到达的时间帧被动态障碍阻挡时不在输入阶段报错：该路线按其时间帧不可达，其他到达时刻仍可参与竞争；末帧之后持续使用最后一帧。
- 搜索保留四邻域移动、禁止等待和回访、进入格子的代价累计。总 `cost` 最小者优先；同价时先比较终点坐标 `(x, y)` 字典序，再比较完整路径字典序。与动态 `plan` 同理，经不同历史到达同一格子的路线是不同状态、互不剪枝；`trace` 在静态模式记录坐标二元组、动态模式记录 `(x, y, t)` 三元组，且只记录实际关闭的节点。
- 没有任何可行终点时 `path`/`cost` 为 `None`；提供预算时按既有规则返回 `status` 为 `found`、`unreachable` 或 `budget_exhausted`，预算不会把已确定的较优路线替换成严格次优（更贵）的路线。`goals` 含 `start` 时按既有 `start == goal` 单点零代价规则处理（零预算同样为 `budget_exhausted`）。

`replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None, dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)` 用于离线核验一条已保存的候选路径并重新计算代价；它不执行搜索，返回值不含 `expanded` 或 `expanded_nodes` 字段，且不接受 `trace` 参数。

**快照与恢复（`snapshot` 与 `resume`）**
- `snapshot` 只能是布尔值，默认 `False`；省略或为 `False` 时 `plan`/`plan_any` 的返回键、值、异常类型、校验顺序、tie-break、不可达结果与轨迹完全不变。非布尔值在全部既有校验（含 `max_expanded` 校验）之后、搜索开始前抛 `TypeError`。
- `snapshot=True` 且本次搜索因达到 `max_expanded` 上限返回 `budget_exhausted` 时，结果额外携带 `checkpoint`；已找到终点或确认不可达的结果不生成该字段。`checkpoint` 只含可 JSON 序列化的值：快照版本、规划器类型（`"plan"`/`"plan_any"`）、规范化网格约束（尺寸、障碍、起终点或候选终点、`costs`、`dynamic_blocked`）、已关闭节点计数、至此的轨迹以及待处理候选的完整状态；所有由集合派生的列表均排序存储，键与值的顺序不受集合迭代、目标列表或帧内坐标顺序影响，调用方可原样保存后传回 `resume`。
- `resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)` 按快照继续同一确定性搜索。`max_expanded` 仍表示从起点累计允许关闭的节点总数：上限不大于已关闭数时不再关闭任何节点。恢复结果的 `path`、`cost`、`expanded`、`status`（仅在提供 `max_expanded` 时返回）与 `expanded_nodes`（恢复结果始终返回；静态模式记录坐标二元组，动态模式记录 `(x, y, t)` 三元组）等价于一次未暂停的调用，重复恢复不会重复计入已关闭节点。再次达到上限时返回新的 `checkpoint`，可继续恢复；最终 `found` 或 `unreachable` 时省略它。恢复成功的路径可直接交给 `replay` 并得到相同代价与步数。
- 校验：`checkpoint` 不是对象、缺少必要字段或字段类型不对时抛 `TypeError`；快照版本、规划器类型、网格约束、障碍、起终点、候选终点、`costs`、`dynamic_blocked` 或内部状态不一致时统一抛 `ValueError`；所有错误在搜索前确定。`resume` 的 `max_expanded` 复用 `plan` 的非负整数规则（其他类型抛 `TypeError`，负数抛 `ValueError`）。

**诊断模式（`diagnose=True`）**
- `diagnose` 只能是布尔值；省略或为 `False` 时，`replay` 的返回键、值、异常类型与校验顺序与默认行为完全一致。非布尔值在全部网格校验（含动态第零帧）完成后、`path` 结构检查之前抛出 `TypeError`。
- 传 `True` 且结构合法时，有效路径仍返回 `valid`、`cost`、`steps`，并额外返回 `"error": None, "error_index": None`；`cost` 仍按进入格子规则重算，`steps == len(path) - 1`。
- 无效路径仍不抛异常，`cost`、`steps` 为 `None`，并返回唯一的 `error` 及首个违规元素的零基 `path` 下标。按固定优先级（同一点同时满足多项时取最前者，且不返回任何部分累计代价）：
  - `start_mismatch`：首点不是 `start`，下标 0；
  - `goal_mismatch`：末点不是 `goal`，下标为末点（`len(path) - 1`）；
  - `start_goal_extra`：`start == goal` 却含多余点，下标 1；
  - `repeated_coordinate`：重复坐标，指向第二次出现的位置；
  - `non_adjacent`：相邻点不是四邻域移动，指向后一个点；
  - `static_blocked`：经过静态障碍，指向该点；
  - `dynamic_blocked`：在对应时间帧（或持续使用的末帧）中被禁行，指向该点。

**replay 返回结构**
- 路径合规时返回 `{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}`：`steps` 为移动边数，恒等于 `len(path) - 1`（`start == goal` 的单点路径为 0）；`cost` 按 `plan` 既有的进入格子规则重算，即路径所进入格子的代价之和，未提供 `costs` 时每步为 1，提供时起点代价不计入，因此与 `plan` 对同一路径给出的代价一致。
- 路径语义不合规时不抛异常，固定返回 `{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`，不返回任何部分累计值。不合规情形包括：未从 `start` 开始、未在 `goal` 结束、经过静态障碍、经过路径下标 `t` 对应的动态障碍帧、相邻点不是四邻域移动、出现重复坐标，以及 `start == goal` 却包含多余点。
- 合规判定与动态时间索引：`dynamic_blocked` 省略、为 `None` 或为空序列时按静态模式检查；否则路径下标 `t` 处的坐标必须避开第 `t` 帧，超过最后一帧后持续使用最后一帧（与 `plan` 的索引规则一致）。

**replay 异常边界（校验先于路径判定）**
- 网格参数（`width`、`height`、`blocked`、`start`、`goal`、`costs`、`dynamic_blocked`）沿用 `plan` 的公开校验与既有 `TypeError`/`ValueError` 边界及顺序，包括 `start` 落在静态障碍或第 0 帧时抛出 `ValueError`；这些校验全部在检查 `path` 之前完成。
- `path` 必须是非空坐标序列：字符串、字节串、`None` 或其他非序列抛出 `TypeError`；空序列抛出 `TypeError`；元素不是恰好两个整数（含长度不为二、非整数、布尔坐标）抛出 `TypeError`；坐标越界抛出 `ValueError`。
- 仅语义上无效（结构合法但不满足上述合规条件）的路径不抛异常，返回固定的无效结构。

**plan 输入校验（搜索开始前完成）** —— replay 的网格参数沿用同一套校验：
- `width`、`height` 必须为正整数。
- `start`、`goal` 及 `blocked` 中每个元素必须是两个整数构成的坐标（元组或长度为二的列表等序列，统一规范化为元组）。
- `costs` 可省略或为 `None`（单位代价）；否则必须是 `height` 行、`width` 列的正整数矩阵（按行排列，`costs[y][x]` 为进入格子 `(x, y)` 的代价）。字符串/字节串、非整数单元格、布尔值抛出 `TypeError`；行数或列数不符、代价非正抛出 `ValueError`。
- `trace` 必须为布尔值，其他类型在搜索开始前抛出 `TypeError`。
- 类型或结构不符抛出 `TypeError`；尺寸非正、坐标越界、端点落在障碍物上抛出 `ValueError`。
- `blocked` 中的重复坐标被合并，不影响结果。

**搜索语义**
- 四邻域移动，曼哈顿启发式。未提供 `costs` 时为单位步长代价；提供时进入格子的代价为该格的值，起点代价不计入，`cost` 等于路径所进入格子的代价之和。
- 平局次序固定且公开：先比较 f，再比较 h，再按 (x, y) 字典序；结果不依赖 `blocked` 的迭代顺序。
- `expanded` 只统计从优先队列取出并首次关闭的节点；成功时计入 goal，`start == goal` 时返回单节点路径、代价 0、`expanded` 为 1；不可达时 `path`/`cost` 为 `None`，`expanded` 等于实际关闭的可通行节点数。

**搜索轨迹（`trace=True`）**
- 成功与不可达结果都额外返回 `expanded_nodes`：坐标元组构成的序列，按节点首次计入 `expanded` 的顺序记录，包含 `start`；成功时包含 `goal`，不可达时记录搜索结束前关闭的全部可通行节点。
- `expanded_nodes` 不含未扩展项、重复坐标或障碍物，且恒有 `expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`；`start == goal` 时序列只有一个坐标。
- `trace=False` 或省略时返回对象不含该字段，其余键、值与校验顺序与默认行为完全一致。

**动态障碍（`dynamic_blocked`）**
- `dynamic_blocked` 省略、为 `None` 或为空序列时与未启用完全等价；否则必须是按时间帧排列的序列，每一帧是该帧禁行坐标的可迭代集合。第 0 帧约束 `start`，路径下标 `t` 处的坐标必须同时避开静态障碍和第 `t` 帧，超过最后一帧后持续使用最后一帧。
- 每一步仍只能向四邻域移动，不允许原地等待或重复坐标；`cost` 仍按进入格子的代价累计，起点不计。由于路线的可延续性取决于它已访问的坐标序列，到达同一 `(x, y, t)` 但历史不同的候选是不同状态，互不剪枝：所有满足约束的路线都能被搜索到。
- 返回总代价最小的可行路径；总代价相同时，固定优先级依次为 f、h、x、y、t，仍相同时按完整坐标路径的字典序决定取舍，因此结果不依赖障碍集合、帧内坐标顺序或遍历顺序。
- 动态模式下 `expanded_nodes` 按实际关闭顺序记录 `(x, y, t)` 三元组，`expanded` 按条目计数；被丢弃的候选不记录。同一 `(x, y, t)` 若由不同历史分别关闭，其三元组按关闭顺序分别出现，`expanded` 逐条计数。不可达时 `path`/`cost` 为 `None`。
- 校验：外层必须是序列，每一帧必须是可迭代坐标集合；字符串/字节串、非二整数坐标抛出 `TypeError`，越界坐标抛出 `ValueError`，帧内重复坐标合并；`start` 在第 0 帧被禁止时抛出 `ValueError`。所有校验在搜索开始前完成，既有校验顺序不变。

content.content:
1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)``,
5	``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, costs=None, trace=False,
6	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)``,
7	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
8	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)`` and
9	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``.
10	
11	Semantics:
12	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
13	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
14	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
15	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
16	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
17	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
18	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
19	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
20	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
21	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
22	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
23	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
24	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
25	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
26	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
27	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
28	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
29	
30	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
31	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
32	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
33	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
34	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
35	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
36	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
37	  check) and before the search starts.
38	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
39	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
40	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
41	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
42	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
43	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
44	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
45	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
46	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
47	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
48	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
49	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
50	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
51	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
52	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
53	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
54	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
55	  accepts no budget parameter.
56	
57	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
58	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
59	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
60	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
61	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
62	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
63	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
64	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
65	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
66	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
67	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
68	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
69	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
70	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
71	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
72	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
73	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
74	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
75	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
76	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
77	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
78	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
79	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
80	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
81	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
82	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
83	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
84	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
85	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
86	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
87	
88	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
89	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
90	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
91	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
92	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
93	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
94	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
95	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
96	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
97	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
98	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
99	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
100	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
101	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
102	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
103	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
104	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
105	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
106	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
107	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
108	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
109	  other arrival times still compete.
110	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
111	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
112	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
113	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
114	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
115	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
116	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
117	  better route with a worse one.
118	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
119	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
120	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
121	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
122	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
123	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
124	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
125	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
126	  and step count.
127	
128	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
129	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
130	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
131	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
132	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
133	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
134	  included) and before the search starts.
135	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
136	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
137	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
138	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
139	  carry the field.
140	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
141	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
142	  candidate goals, costs and dynamic frames), the closed-node count, the
143	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
144	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
145	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
146	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
147	  back to ``resume`` later.
148	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
149	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
150	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
151	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
152	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
153	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
154	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
155	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
156	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
157	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
158	  closed node twice.
159	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
160	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
161	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
162	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
163	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
164	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
165	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
166	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
167	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
168	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
169	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
170	
171	Offline replay (``replay``):
172	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
173	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
174	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
175	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
176	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
177	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
178	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
179	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
180	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
181	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
182	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
183	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
184	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
185	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
186	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
187	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
188	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
189	  ``start == goal``.
190	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
191	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
192	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
193	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
194	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
195	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
196	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
197	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
198	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
199	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
200	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
201	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
202	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
203	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
204	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
205	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
206	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
207	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
208	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
209	  ever returned.
210	
211	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
212	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
213	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
214	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
215	  normalized to tuples.
216	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
217	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
218	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
219	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
220	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
221	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
222	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
223	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
224	"""

239	def _is_int(value):
240	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

243	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
244	    if not _is_int(value):
245	        raise TypeError(
246	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
247	        )
248	    if value <= 0:
249	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {value}")
250	    return value

253	def _normalize_point(value, name):
254	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
255	        raise TypeError(
256	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
257	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
258	        )
259	    if len(value) != 2:
260	        raise TypeError(
261	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
262	        )
263	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
264	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
265	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
266	    return (x, y)

269	def _check_bounds(point, width, height, name):
270	    x, y = point
271	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
272	        raise ValueError(
273	            f"{name} {point} is outside the {width}x{height} grid"
274	        )

277	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
278	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
279	        raise TypeError(
280	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
281	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
282	        )
283	    cells = set()
284	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
285	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
286	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
287	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
288	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
289	    return cells

292	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
293	    if costs is None:
294	        return None  # unit step cost
295	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
296	        raise TypeError(
297	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
298	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
299	        )
300	    if len(costs) != height:
301	        raise ValueError(
302	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
303	        )
304	    rows = []
305	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
306	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
307	            raise TypeError(
308	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
309	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
310	            )
311	        if len(row) != width:
312	            raise ValueError(
313	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
314	                f"got {len(row)}"
315	            )
316	        parsed = []
317	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
318	            if not _is_int(cell):
319	                raise TypeError(
320	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
321	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
322	                )
323	            if cell <= 0:
324	                raise ValueError(
325	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
326	                    f"got {cell}"
327	                )
328	            parsed.append(cell)
329	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
330	    return tuple(rows)

333	def _normalize_dynamic_blocked(dynamic_blocked, width, height):
334	    if dynamic_blocked is None:
335	        return None  # dynamic mode disabled
336	    if isinstance(dynamic_blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
337	        dynamic_blocked, Sequence
338	    ):
339	        raise TypeError(
340	            f"dynamic_blocked must be a sequence of frames, "
341	            f"got {type(dynamic_blocked).__name__}"
342	        )
343	    if len(dynamic_blocked) == 0:
344	        return None  # no frames: equivalent to not provided
345	    frames = []
346	    for t, frame in enumerate(dynamic_blocked):
347	        if isinstance(frame, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(frame, Iterable):
348	            raise TypeError(
349	                f"dynamic_blocked[{t}] must be an iterable of grid "
350	                f"coordinates, got {type(frame).__name__}"
351	            )
352	        cells = set()
353	        for index, item in enumerate(frame):
354	            name = f"dynamic_blocked[{t}][{index}]"
355	            point = _normalize_point(item, name)
356	            _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
357	            cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
358	        frames.append(frozenset(cells))
359	    return frames

363	    if (path is None or isinstance(path, (str, bytes))
364	            or not isinstance(path, Sequence)):
365	        raise TypeError(
366	            f"path must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
367	            f"got {type(path).__name__}"
368	        )
369	    if len(path) == 0:
370	        raise TypeError("path must be a non-empty sequence of coordinates")
371	    points = []

373	        name = f"path[{index}]"

380	def _normalize_goals(goals):
381	    # ``goals`` is the plan_any counterpart of ``plan``'s single ``goal``.
382	    # This performs the outer/structure pass in exactly the position where
383	    # ``plan`` structurally normalizes ``goal``: strings, bytes, ``None``
384	    # and other non-sequences are ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a
385	    # ``ValueError``; every element is normalized to a coordinate tuple
386	    # (element shape/coordinate type failures are ``TypeError``). Bounds and
387	    # obstacle checks follow in ``plan_any`` at the same relative positions
388	    # ``plan`` uses for its single goal. Duplicates merge and the tuple is
389	    # sorted so the input order never affects the result.
390	    if (goals is None or isinstance(goals, (str, bytes))
391	            or not isinstance(goals, Sequence)):
392	        raise TypeError(
393	            f"goals must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
394	            f"got {type(goals).__name__}"
395	        )
396	    if len(goals) == 0:
397	        raise ValueError("goals must contain at least one candidate endpoint")
398	    points = set()
399	    for index, item in enumerate(goals):
400	        point = _normalize_point(item, f"goals[{index}]")
401	        points.add(point)
402	    return tuple(sorted(points))

429	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
430	                   max_expanded, snapshot=False, state=None):
431	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
432	
433	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
434	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
435	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
436	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
437	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
438	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
439	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
440	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
441	    """
442	
443	    def heuristic(point):
444	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
445	
446	    def step_cost(point):
447	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
448	        if costs is None:
449	            return 1
450	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
451	
452	    if state is None:
453	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
454	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
455	        # is never compared.
456	        h0 = heuristic(start)
457	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
458	        came_from = {}
459	        g_score = {start: 0}
460	        closed = set()
461	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
462	    else:
463	        open_heap = state["open"]
464	        came_from = state["came_from"]
465	        g_score = state["g_score"]
466	        closed = state["closed"]
467	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
468	    budget_stop = False
469	
470	    while open_heap:
471	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
472	        current = entry[4]
473	        if current in closed:
474	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
475	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
476	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
477	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
478	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
479	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
480	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
481	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
482	            budget_stop = True
483	            if snapshot:
484	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)
485	            break
486	        closed.add(current)
487	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
488	            expanded_nodes.append(current)
489	        if current == goal:
490	            path = [current]
491	            while path[-1] in came_from:
492	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])
493	            path.reverse()
494	            result = {
495	                "path": path,
496	                "cost": g_score[current],
497	                "expanded": len(closed),
498	            }
499	            if max_expanded is not None:
500	                result["status"] = "found"
501	            if trace:
502	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
503	            return result
504	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
505	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
506	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):
507	                continue
508	            if nxt in obstacles:
509	                continue
510	            new_g = g_score[current] + step_cost(nxt)
511	            if new_g < g_score.get(nxt, float("inf")):
512	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
513	                came_from[nxt] = current
514	                h = heuristic(nxt)
515	                heapq.heappush(
516	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
517	                )
518	    result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": len(closed)}
519	    if max_expanded is not None:
520	        result["status"] = (
521	            "budget_exhausted" if budget_stop else "unreachable"
522	        )
523	    if trace:
524	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
525	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
526	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
527	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, None,
528	            len(closed), expanded_nodes,
529	            _static_snapshot_state(open_heap, came_from, g_score, closed),
530	        )
531	    return result
532

534	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
535	                    trace, max_expanded, snapshot=False, state=None):
536	    """History-sensitive time-expanded A*.
537	
538	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
539	    past the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting in place and repeated
540	    coordinates are forbidden, so whether a candidate route can be
541	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
542	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
543	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
544	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
545	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
546	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
547	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
548	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
549	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
550	    lexicographic order. With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally
551	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
552	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
553	    """
554	
555	    def heuristic(point):
556	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
557	
558	    def step_cost(point):
559	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
560	        if costs is None:
561	            return 1
562	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
563	
564	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1
565	
566	    def frame_cells(t):
567	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
568	
569	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
570	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
571	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
572	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
573	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
574	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).
575	    if state is None:
576	        h0 = heuristic(start)
577	        start_path = (start,)
578	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], 0, 0, start_path,
579	                      frozenset(start_path))]
580	        closed_count = 0
581	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None

795	def _snapshot_checkpoint(planner, width, height, obstacles, start, endpoints,

797	    # The checkpoint is built from JSON-native values only (ints, strings,

804	        "width": width,

810	        checkpoint["goal"] = [endpoints[0], endpoints[1]]

812	        checkpoint["goals"] = [[goal[0], goal[1]] for goal in endpoints]

814	        [list(row) for row in costs] if costs is not None else None

846	def _tree_snapshot_state(open_heap, best_key, planner):
847	    # The complete route-tree state: every live candidate with its full

861	        "open": [
862	            [f, h, x, y, t, g, [[point[0], point[1]] for point in path]]
863	            for f, h, x, y, t, g, path, _seen in open_heap
